Alice —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions and for looping in legal. Short answers up front:

• Training: By default for our Hosted API, Redwood does not include customer request/response data in model training datasets or downstream model updates. We consider customer data non-training data unless explicit opt-in is documented in a contract.

• Logs & snapshots: Operational telemetry (metrics, aggregated latencies) is retained for platform health. Request-level debug logs, KV cache snapshots, and persistent diagnostics are retained only as needed for operational troubleshooting and are scoped by contract (default short retention, longer if requested).

I attached two items: a short explainer PDF and a retention matrix that shows default windows and what changes under Dedicated/Private deployments. If helpful, I can pull Prioym from Security to provide the exact clause wording we recommend for procurement paperwork.

Next steps: Do you want a one-paragraph warranty statement we can insert into the Master Services Agreement plus a fallback operational retention table?

Ben / team —

Thanks for flagging. Quick clarifications and recommended contract language below. High level: the "we do not train" statement is accurate for customer content under our standard Hosted terms, with the following important nuances that procurement usually asks about:

1) Telemetry vs. content: Aggregate telemetry (e.g., token-level latency distributions, error rates) is used to monitor and optimize platform performance and is not used to fine-tune customer-facing language models. We explicitly segregate telemetry from datasets used in model training pipelines.

2) Debug logs & snapshots: Default Hosted retention: request-level debug logs retained for 30 days (deleted sooner on request), KV cache snapshots kept for 90 days for cache warm-up and routing efficiency. Backups/snapshots for disaster recovery are retained for up to 180 days and are encrypted and access-controlled.

3) Dedicated & Private: Dedicated customers can request custom retention (SLA-dependent) — typical options are 7, 30, or 90 days for logs and snapshots; backups still retained per the contract but can be configured. Private deployments are customer-managed; Redwood provides tooling and recommended defaults but does not have access unless explicitly configured.

4) Forensics & legal holds: We will honor lawful requests/holds; these create exceptions to deletion timelines and are logged and audited as part of our compliance processes.

Suggested MSA language (single sentence + qualifier):
"Redwood will not use Customer-provided content, request/response data, or derived conversational artifacts to train models or create model weights without the Customer's prior written consent. Aggregate platform telemetry for operational monitoring may be retained and used internally, but such telemetry is segregated and not included in model training datasets."

I'll also attach the SOC2 control extract and a short ops note. Let me know if you want this tightened by Legal.
